_README: Dashboard config (NOT secrets). This is where targets/goals live, read at runtime by lib/metrics.ps1 - never hard-code a business target in code.
_payrollCompleteness_README: M4 overtime: a day's payroll is flagged incomplete when its total gross-pay-item count is below this fraction of the median same-weekday count over the prior N weeks (N = payrollCompletenessLookbackWeeks).
_callBoard_README: Call Board: any HVAC/ROPPS/Plumbing call whose jobTypeId is in nonOpportunityJobTypeIds is shown but EXCLUDED from the headline opportunity count. Edit this list (ServiceTitan job-type IDs) to change what counts as a non-opportunity - no code change needed. The Call Board fails loud (on-screen error) if any ID here is not a real job type. Current 10: Recall/Warranty, Install HVAC Part 1-2 HRS, Install HVAC Part 4-5 HRS, Plumbing Part Install 3-5 HRS, Filter Change 1-7 Yrs, Filter Change 8+, Commercial Cooling/Heating Issue, Commercial Cooling/Heating Maintenance, Commercial Install HVAC Part, Drive By.
_siloFlip_README: SILO flip rate = (TGLs created) / (ROPP calls ran), the SILO manager's own definition. It is built from two ServiceTitan saved reports, and NOTHING about them is hard-coded in code - if a report is renamed, re-saved under a new id, or has a column added/removed/reordered, you fix it HERE. numerator = report 642925621 'ROPP TGLS CREATED (JOHN)' (category technician, DateType 3 = the window applies to ScheduledDate); the TGL count is simply how many rows it returns for the period. denominator = report 379143819 'Johns Copy of Ericka's Revenue by Job Type' (category accounting, DateType 1 = the window applies to CompletionDate); the calls-ran count is how many of its rows survive cleaning. expectedColumns is the tripwire: the metric asserts the report returns EXACTLY these column names in EXACTLY this order and errors on screen if not, because both reports are one person's personal copies and an edit to either would otherwise shift our number silently. dateColumn / jobNumberColumn name (never index) the two columns the math needs. tags.managementRemoved (545867780) and tags.ropp (962027) are the ServiceTitan job tags the denominator cleaning rules test: a Management-Removed job is dropped, and a job without the ROPP tag is dropped. THREE PERIODS are reported: TODAY (Pacific), month-to-date and year-to-date, each from its own server-side windowed pull of both reports - so a full build is 6 report POSTs, never a client-side re-slice of one big pull. targetRate (60) is the flip-rate target the dashboard colour-codes each period against: at or above it reads as on-target, below it does not. It lives here and ONLY here - the dashboard reads the number out of the saved figure instead of having 60 written into the page, so moving the goal is a one-number edit in this file with no code change. It is a percentage, so it must be greater than 0 and no more than 100; anything else is a loud error rather than a quietly-ignored setting. postSpacingSeconds is how long to wait between report POSTs - this tenant 429-throttles rapid report runs with a ~60s cooldown, so 65 is deliberate; lowering it just makes the run slower via retries. THE TWO FRESHNESS CLOCKS ARE SEPARATE ON PURPOSE, because the periods go stale at wildly different speeds. cacheTtlSeconds (21600 = 6 hours) is the clock for a FULL rebuild of all three periods: refresh-silo-flip.ps1 skips that ~7-8 minute recompute (6 throttled report POSTs plus a ~42,000-job pull covering the whole year) until data/silo-flip.json is older than this, which is what keeps the every-15-minutes CI refresh fast. Six hours is fine for a year-to-date figure built on ~4,900 calls - a few more calls barely move it. todayTtlSeconds (1800 = 30 minutes) is the MUCH SHORTER clock for today's figure alone, which goes stale in minutes: on a 20-call day a single TGL swings it several points, so a 6-hour-old 'today' number is simply wrong by mid-afternoon. It gets its own clock because refreshing today ALONE is cheap - 2 report POSTs plus a one-day jobs pull of a few hundred jobs, about 1-2 minutes - so it can run many times a day while the expensive full rebuild stays rare. When today's clock expires but the 6-hour clock has not, the script recomputes only today and carries the stored month-to-date and year-to-date figures forward untouched. Lower todayTtlSeconds for a livelier number at the cost of more API pressure; raise it if 429s appear. errorRetryCooldownSeconds (3600 = 1 hour) is a THIRD, separate clock used when the last build FAILED: a failed build still writes a status='error' block, and we want it retried sooner than 6 hours but NOT by every 15-minute CI run. Retrying every run means the full 6 throttled report POSTs plus a ~42k-job pull each time, on top of the 3 report POSTs refresh.ps1 already makes in the same run - which is how the tenant got stuck 429-throttled on 2026-08-11 instead of recovering. A failed cache is always retried with a FULL rebuild, never a today-only one, because there is no trustworthy month-to-date/year-to-date figure left to carry forward. Raise it if 429s persist; lower it to recover faster at the cost of more API pressure. Every key above is REQUIRED - a missing one is a loud error, never a default.
